title: Iran's two-day offer, a busy night at sea, and Ukraine's oil campaign widens
summary: Iran offers to reopen Hormuz within two days on its terms as three more vessels are hit around the Gulf, Ukraine strikes a major Russian oil hub after three refineries, Russia's overnight drone attacks, Sudan's power grid under fire, and China's coast guard patrols east of Taiwan.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Welcome to the ForceFinder Daily Briefing. I'm Avery.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And I'm Cole. As always, this show is generated automatically from the open-source reporting behind the ForceFinder map. Every story has source links on the globe, so treat us as a guide, not the final word.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: It's Monday, November second. The day before the US midterms. And the big story is a new offer from Tehran.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Right. Iran says it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days. But only if Washington agrees to a list of conditions.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And it's quite a list. Unfreezing Iranian assets abroad. Ending the US naval blockade of Iranian ports. Lifting sanctions. And ending the war on all fronts.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: There's also a new channel. Iran's security chief says he received a letter from Vice President JD Vance, seeking to revive talks. He says he hasn't answered it yet. Messages are going back and forth through mediators, with Qatar still hosting talks in Doha.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And President Trump's line today was that the war will end very soon, quote, one way or the other.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Which is the tension in one sentence, right? Diplomacy on one track. And on the other, US officials have reportedly told allies to be ready for renewed strikes after tomorrow's vote.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Meanwhile, at sea, it was a rough night. Let's go through it, because there were three separate incidents reported by the British maritime agency, UKMTO, and by security firms.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: First, a tanker was hit on its port side by an unknown projectile, about forty nautical miles south of Iran's Lavan Island. That's in the Gulf itself, well west of the strait. There was a fire, but the crew was reported safe.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Second, inside the strait, an offshore tug called the Selat Storm was struck by a projectile and partially sank. That's according to the maritime security firm Vanguard Tech.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And third, late on Sunday, a tanker was hit by two projectiles about seventy-two nautical miles east of Ras Al Khafji. That's off the Saudi coast, up near Kuwait. All the crew were accounted for.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And then on top of that, Iran's Revolutionary Guard navy claims two more tankers, including a supertanker, exploded after hitting mines on what it calls an unauthorised route.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Important caveat there. It's not clear whether those are the same ships UKMTO reported, and the mine claims haven't been independently verified. Central Command has said for days that the main lanes are cleared of mines, and that Iran is using missiles and drones instead.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: So the incidents are real. Who did what, and how, is still disputed.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Let's go to Ukraine, because the energy war there keeps widening.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Yesterday we talked about three Russian refineries in three nights. Today, drones hit something different. A Transneft pumping and blending station near Prosvet, in Samara region. Russian independent media describe it as one of Europe's largest oil transport hubs. It's where Urals export crude gets blended.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Local authorities confirmed an attack, but gave no details on damage. And Ukraine hasn't claimed it. One outlet notes it's the first strike on that hub since October eleventh.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Why does that matter? Because refineries make fuel for Russia's own use. An export blending hub is about the oil Russia sells abroad. So it's a step toward Russia's income, not just its supply.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And it lands in a tricky spot politically. The Wall Street Journal had reported that the US pressed Kyiv to pause these attacks, partly over fuel prices. That pause looks well and truly over.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And Russia's strikes on Ukraine continued overnight too. Ukraine's air force says Russia launched one hundred and ninety-three drones, and a hundred and fifty-four were shot down. In Sloviansk, in Donetsk region, the governor says one person was killed.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: In the Kharkiv region, a drone attack on the village of Vashyshcheve injured twelve people, including a child. And the Kyiv Independent reports strikes on energy infrastructure left ten regions facing power outages.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: On the front line, Ukraine's General Staff counted two hundred and five clashes on Sunday. The Pokrovsk sector was again the hottest.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And that small six-day ceasefire around the occupied town of Oleshky, in Kherson region, has now ended. It held without reported violations, and it let aid in and some residents out. People in Kherson are now bracing for the fighting to return.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: One odd story to flag. Ukraine's air raid alert app was hacked and sent out false warnings. Hours later, Russia said its own emergency warning app was hit by a, quote, massive cyberattack. Ukraine blamed Russia for the first one.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Okay, quick lap of the other fronts. Lebanon. L'Orient Today reports intense Israeli air raids and artillery fire on southern Lebanon overnight into Monday, including the villages of Kfar Tibnit and Qsair, near Nabatieh.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: In Gaza, local health officials say Israeli strikes killed at least four people today. The Israeli military says it targeted militants.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: Yemen. The Saudi-led coalition says it carried out a precision operation against Houthi resources used to attack Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping. Houthi-linked media reported two strikes on the University of Hodeida. And the UN says more than three hundred thousand people have now fled their homes in western Yemen.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: Sudan's power grid is taking a beating. Drones knocked the Al Dabbah and Abu Hamad power stations in the north out of service on Sunday. Sudan Tribune counts fourteen power stations hit in two weeks. A lawyers' group and the government blame the Rapid Support Forces.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: And in Darfur, the army's drones are active too. Darfur twenty-four reports an army drone strike on a vehicle in Al-Malha, which the Rapid Support Forces control, killed two people.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: And finally, Taiwan. China's coast guard says it ran routine law enforcement patrols in the waters east of Taiwan on Saturday. Taiwan's coast guard calls that harassment of shipping, and Taiwanese officials think China may be practising for a maritime blockade.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: On the ships, no change today. The newest public fleet report is still from late October. The George Washington and the George H. W. Bush are in the Arabian Sea. And the Theodore Roosevelt and the Makin Island groups are reportedly headed for the Middle East, but there's no new confirmed position yet.

segments.speaker: Avery
segments.text: So, what to watch. The midterms tomorrow, and whether the US answers Iran's two-day offer or chooses the other path. Whether that new fleet tracker shows the Roosevelt heading west. And whether Ukraine keeps going after Russia's oil exports.

segments.speaker: Cole
segments.text: That's the briefing. Thanks for listening, and we'll see you tomorrow.
